key_insight: A basin-scale tracer-flux framework links thermohaline circulation tipping to the balance between nonlinear advection and linear dissipation.
engineering_relevance: Transport-budget diagnostics could improve ocean-model stability assessment by revealing proximity to tipping that overturning strength alone cannot show.
method: Derive a tracer-conservation balance between surface fluxes, dissipation, and advection.
Describe transport using large-scale tracer gradients and efficiency relative to a no-flow conductive state.
Evaluate a three-dimensional basin model and connect weak- and strong-flow regimes to box-model bifurcations.
evidence_signal: In the three-dimensional basin model, nonlinear salinity advection dominates the collapse threshold, while linear dissipation dominates recovery.
watch_item: The abstract reports idealized basin-model results, not validation against observed ocean tipping; forecasting closures are deferred to Part II.
paper_title: Basin-Scale Nonlinear Dynamics of Thermohaline Ocean Circulation. Part I: Theory
